candidate.title: PEAT
candidate.scope: The single PEAT (Paired-end analysis of transcription start sites) row of the assigned Illumina poster, interpreted at schematic scope using the Ni et al. 2010 oligo-capping/MmeI paired-tag implementation. The drawn route starts with capped polyadenylated mRNA and ends with restriction-generated cDNA; primary-paper context identifies the tag carrier and the subsequent sequencing interface without adding unshown preparation operations. Adjacent TIF-Seq, SMORE-Seq, partial upper-row content, and right-side chemical legend are neighboring catalogue context, not alternative PEAT workflows.

states.label: Capped, polyadenylated mRNA
features: Biological target is the 5′ end of mRNA; the poster represents the starting RNA with a 5′ GPPP cap symbol, a purple RNA body, and AA(A)n at the 3′ end.
The separate transcript icon beside the PEAT name summarizes the target and is not an additional material-processing branch.
The matched implementation uses poly(A)+ RNA; the poster begins after any upstream RNA enrichment.

states.label: Linear double-stranded paired-tag cDNA
features: Final cDNA is drawn as two parallel blue strands with green/orange internal linker segments.
Primary implementation recovers a 93–95 bp MmeI fragment carrying an approximately 20 nt original-5′-end tag paired with an approximately 20 nt downstream tag.
The downstream tag reflects the random RT priming position, not a defined polyadenylation-site tag.
Distinct built-in linker sequences identify the two tag origins in the eventual paired-end readout.
This depicted product precedes the sequencing-adapter ligation described in the paper.

The intended pairing is between two regions of one copied RNA segment. The secondary catalogue notes possible chimeric fragments, so the schematic linkage does not guarantee that every recovered pair represents a native same-RNA association.

operations.label: Tobacco acid pyrophosphatase (TAP) treatment
operations.description: Removes the cap from the depicted capped mRNA, yielding the RNA with the 5′ P end shown before linker ligation; the RNA body and poly(A) tail remain.
operations.mechanism: TAP-mediated decapping, as drawn. The Ni implementation also reports BAP dephosphorylation before TAP; that omitted upstream operation is recorded as interpretation context in the correction, not inserted into this route.
operations.information_effect: Exposes the original capped RNA 5′ position for linker attachment. TAP alone in this drawing does not establish discrimination against every pre-existing uncapped RNA end.

operations.label: Reverse transcription with random primers
operations.description: Copies the linker-bearing RNA from a random priming position toward its 5′ end. The resulting first-strand cDNA carries MmeI-bearing linker sequences at both ends, one from RNA ligation and one from the primer.
operations.mechanism: Random-hexamer-initiated reverse transcription with a primer tail containing the second MmeI site.
operations.information_effect: Transfers RNA sequence into the DNA readout carrier while associating its original 5′ end with a downstream position on the copied RNA segment. Random priming determines which downstream region can become the partner tag.

operations.label: PCR amplify and circularize
operations.description: Amplifies the first-strand cDNA and joins its ends into circular DNA. The primary paper resolves the material sequence within this combined poster block: PCR produces blunt double-stranded DNA, then collector/bridge ligation produces single-stranded circular DNA.
operations.mechanism: PCR followed by collector/bridge-mediated circularization, kept as the single combined operation depicted.
operations.information_effect: Amplifies the copied RNA segment and brings its 5′-linker and random-primer-linker ends together in one circular molecule. That junction makes the two short transcript-derived end tags recoverable together.

operations.label: Restriction endonuclease
operations.description: MmeI digestion of the RCA material releases the short linear double-stranded cDNA product drawn at the end of the row. The recovered fragment contains the linked 5′-end and downstream tags rather than the full copied RNA segment.
operations.mechanism: The poster names only restriction endonuclease; its two MmeI site labels and the primary paper identify the enzyme as MmeI. The primary implementation recovers the 93–95 bp paired-tag fragment.
operations.information_effect: The same DNA fragment carries a 5′ RNA-end tag and its downstream partner, supporting paired-end mapping of RNA 5′ positions to genes and local transcript structure after the unshown sequencing-adapter interface. Linker identity distinguishes tag direction. A capped RNA 5′ position is not by itself proof of de novo initiation: the primary study also reports internally recapped transcripts.

method_scopes.rationale: PEAT is the only assigned target. The named row supplies all six operations as one unbranched route. The verified catalogue page is headed PEAT: Paired-end Analysis of Transcription Start Sites and repeats the same operations; Ni et al. explicitly describes the matching two-MmeI-site, random-primed, circularization/RCA strategy. Oligo-capping is a component of this PEAT implementation, not a separate target. The source circle and paired-tag chemistry are resolved from full text; BAP is upstream interpretation context only. This extraction does not assert that every assay called PEAT has identical preparation. The collection page is secondary evidence; its cited plant application and reviews do not establish additional targets or complete experimental equivalence. The in-scope poster reference is Ni et al., verified against publication metadata and the inspected full-text methods.

corrections.diagram_observation: The PEAT row starts with capped mRNA and depicts TAP treatment yielding a 5′ P RNA; it does not depict BAP pretreatment or competing uncapped RNA. The matched secondary collection page additionally says that capped and noncapped RNA are not distinguished.
corrections.primary_statement: Ni et al. explicitly reports BAP dephosphorylation before TAP and describes PEAT oligo-capping as selective ligation of capped transcripts. Accordingly, the primary implementation supports an enrichment for originally capped RNA in the stated BAP/TAP preparation. The local operation remains the TAP-only transformation actually drawn. The diagram alone neither establishes the full cap-selection preparation nor proves perfect cap specificity; the catalogue disadvantage is not a reliable universal description of the Ni implementation.
